SITIONS = {('new','paid'), ('new','cancelled'), ('paid','refunded')}` — the semantics written out literally.
- `can_transition(old, new)` — identical behavior to the contract: membership test in `ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS`.
- `consume(old, new)` — the requested entry point: returns `{"ok", "old", "new", "contract_version", "reason"}`, and on illegal transitions adds `reason="illegal_transition"` plus `allowed_from` (sorted legal successors of `old`). `ok` is exactly `can_transition(old,new)`.
- A `__main__` self-check block asserting v2 behavior (`new→paid`, `new→cancelled`, `paid→refunded` allowed; `new→refunded`, `paid→new`, `refunded→paid`, `cancelled→paid`, `new→new` rejected) and checking `consume` output.

Note: I attempted small local checks via the runner, but it refused every command form ("only python commands allowed") without executing, so no runtime verification result was obtained; the enclosed `if __name__ == "__main__"` block performs that check when the file is run directly.
